title: Cleanliness and the shop's standing
summary: Supermarket Simulator watches how clean the shop is: the game ties cleanliness to the shop's standing, so a messy floor is recorded rather than merely inconvenient.
body: Cleanliness is tracked by the game against the shop's standing, which is why cleaning is part of running the shop rather than a side chore.
Because it is a tracked value rather than a visual effect, how the shop looks can matter beyond the moment you tidy it.
Everything else on this page about reputation, reviews and their effect is not something we could verify, so we do not describe it here.
What this entry does not tell you: how much cleanliness affects anything, how fast the shop gets dirty, or what customers do about it. We have not verified those numbers, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: Cleanliness is tracked against the shop's standing.
The game keeps a store controller for the market side of the shop.
The build keeps a cached cleanup record of its own.
The mop is named twice over in the build, alongside a controller for mopping and a sound effect that goes with it.
facts.evidence: asset names: SM_Mop, SM_Mop_1, MopCleaningController, Mop Cleaning SFX

facts.claim: Trash is named per product line, and for some lines the build carries two spellings of the same name.
facts.evidence: asset names: SM_Trash_Apple Juice_Bio Juice, SM_Trash_Apple_Juice_Bio_Juice, SM_TrashPasta Spaghetti_Elo, SM_TrashPasta_Spaghetti_Elo
